WHAT THIS PHASE PROVED, AND THE DEFECT IT FOUND. Phase 6 governed Dead Aisle, a real external project, through the signed installed Control Centre. The pilot found a defect self-hosting could not: the packaged daemon is launched with its working directory set to the runtime payload root, which is not a repository, so gitBoundSystem bound the git EXECUTABLE but never the DIRECTORY. Every call naming its repository with -C <root> kept working; every ambient call ran in the payload root and failed closed, surfacing to the owner as REPOSITORY_FACTS_UNAVAILABLE and blocking both plan.draft and plan.activate. The correction d188ef7 binds the governed project root at the one seam every git call already passes through: an explicit options.cwd still wins, an argv -C still wins over both because git acts on it first, and a non-absolute root is refused rather than resolved ambiently. Proven by A/B against the real daemon under packaged conditions: pre-fix REPOSITORY_FACTS_UNAVAILABLE for both flows, post-fix code 0 with the correct repository, branch and HEAD. The plan.activate half of that A/B was re-run in a genuinely isolated repository after an earlier sandbox proved unsound.

THE CRLF TRAP RECURRED, AND WAS FIXED BY RE-MATERIALISING RATHER THAN EDITING. The first subject-bound run returned 125/129. All four failures were line-ending drift, not defects at this commit: this repository still has NO .gitattributes while core.autocrlf is true, so a fresh worktree materialises CRLF, and several checks pin LF bytes. Proven rather than assumed - docs/architecture/projectos-v3-master-plan.md hashed 392420ed50756344 on disk against the committed 7bd6235f5f5d948c, and the validator reported that exact CRLF digest; node-v24.14.1-SHASUMS256.txt hashed 46eaca259f8b32ba against the committed cbbb0113ad929e40. Two further failures came from validator regexes containing a literal \n that cannot match \r\n. The worktree was re-created with core.autocrlf=false and every affected file verified BYTE-IDENTICAL to its committed blob before the recorded run. No validator was modified, no source was edited, no check was excluded or weakened. The missing .gitattributes remains carry-forward, deliberately not fixed during this phase.

BOUNDARY-DRIFT INCIDENT, RECORDED RATHER THAN TIDIED AWAY. While building a test sandbox the implementer copied Dead Aisle with cp -r. Dead Aisle is a LINKED WORKTREE, so its .git is a file pointing at the original repository; the copy shared that repository and TWO COMMITS LANDED ON THE REAL DEAD AISLE BRANCH while a no-commit gate was in force. The implementer detected it, reported it unprompted, and reversed it fully: nothing was pushed because no upstream is configured, both commits were reversed, and Dead Aisle was restored to a2f5122a4338 with a working-tree status byte-identical to the reconciliation snapshot. The affected proof was then repeated in a genuinely isolated repository created with git init after excluding .git at copy time, with isolation verified against the original before anything ran. Gatekeeper disposition: BOUNDARY DRIFT - RECOVERED, NON-BLOCKING - NO FURTHER ACTION. The reflogs and unreferenced objects are DELIBERATELY PRESERVED as evidence; no gc, no reflog expiry, no deletion.
